title: Payment fraud falls by £73m following PSR reimbursement scheme
date_evidence: 01/07/2026 (date shown on the PSR news item)
key_claim: The PSR's independent evaluation estimates UK APP fraud losses fell by about £73 million a year after mandatory reimbursement, with firms reimbursing 97% of in-scope claims, and calls for a step-change from tech firms and telcos.
frame_summary: The regulator presents mandatory reimbursement as working and then turns the remaining responsibility toward technology and telecoms firms.
verbatim_quote: APP fraud losses have fallen by an estimated £73 million per year
verbatim_list: firms are now reimbursing 97%
a step-change in the approach taken by tech firms and telcos
A consultation, launching before the end of the year, will include proposals to improve consistency in the application of the policy.
notes: Fetched via WebFetch 05/10/2026 in two passes; date line read from page. Quotes manually verified (device network cannot reach psr.org.uk).

title: APP scams reimbursement dashboard for Q1 2026

title: APP fraud reimbursement requirement: were industry's concerns justified?
key_claim: Adjusting the PSR evaluation for slower-emerging scams and international displacement cuts the year-one net benefit from £17m to £29m to between -£4m and £8m; platforms and telecoms are linked to a large share of incidents and losses but the PSR cannot compel them.
frame_summary: The advisory firm accepts the evaluation's headline but argues the net benefit is fragile once displacement is counted, and that the costs and the fraud origins sit in different sectors.
verbatim_quote: Taken together, these two adjustments imply a net benefit of -£4m to £8m, rather than the £17m to £29m headline figure.
verbatim_list: Losses to crypto exchanges increased more than two-and-a-half times over the same period, from approximately £59m to £153m.
Meta platforms were linked to 54% of 2023 scam incidents and 18% of losses.
Telecoms, meanwhile, were linked to just 12% of cases but 31.5% of losses.
three firms saw materially larger increases, including one equivalent to 2.6% of revenue
The evaluation found no evidence either had happened at scale.
has no powers to compel their cooperation
intends to consult on new annual reporting requirements covering the platforms and services that fraudsters use to reach victims
notes: Three WebFetch passes on 05/10/2026; each quote re-read. Counter-evidence source.

title: Deception in the AI Age 2026
key_claim: Victims' losses from financial scams reached about $20 billion in 2025, up 26%; current liability structures leave banks, telecoms and platforms each seeing only part of a scam, and the UK splits liability 50/50 between sending and receiving institutions.
frame_summary: The research institute argues that scams cross sectors while liability stays inside one, so no single party has the incentive or the view to stop them.
verbatim_quote: Victims' losses from financial scams reached approximately $20 billion in 2025, a 26% increase from the prior year.
verbatim_list: Under the UK model, liability is split 50/50 between sending and receiving institutions.
Banks see the money moving, and meta platforms see the grooming and early contact.
notes: Report landing page fetched twice on 05/10/2026.

title: EU RegCORE client alert: the PSR and PSD3 move forward (April 2026)
key_claim: The EU payments package makes the PSP refund bank-impersonation scams in full, obliges electronic communications providers to prevent impersonation fraud, requires very large platforms to verify regulated financial advertisers, and applies 21 months after entry into force subject to formal adoption.
frame_summary: The advisory alert presents the EU package as extending fraud duties beyond payment firms to telecoms and platforms, with timing contingent on formal adoption.
verbatim_quote: Where a consumer is manipulated by a fraudster pretending to be the consumer's PSP, using communication channels attributed to that PSP, the PSP must refund the full amount of the resulting fraudulent authorised transaction.
verbatim_list: Electronic communications services providers must take appropriate measures to detect and prevent the use of their services for impersonation fraud, including manipulation of calling line identification.
must request authorisation or registration details from advertisers of regulated financial services and make best efforts to verify these details before permitting advertisements
both instruments will apply 21 months after entry into force
notes: Structural anchor (3-6m band). The PDF gives month and year only ('April 2026'); 30/04/2026 is a month-end placeholder day, and the alert itself refers to the Council's 23 April 2026 release, so it was written on or after that date. Flagged to analyst.

title: Banks, telcos and digital platforms are now legally accountable for scam prevention
key_claim: Australia's scam regime puts duties on banks, telecoms and digital platforms with fines up to $50 million per contravention, SPF rules from 1 September 2026, AFCA complaint handling from 1 January 2027 and a proposed $3,000 automatic reimbursement threshold.
frame_summary: The trade report describes Australia as having made scam prevention a legal duty across banks, telecoms and platforms rather than a banking-only obligation.
verbatim_quote: Fines of up to $50 million per contravention apply for failure to meet obligations under the framework.
verbatim_list: The SPF Rules commence on 1 September 2026.
A proposed $3,000 automatic reimbursement threshold for verified scam losses below that amount is included in the Treasury's draft sector codes.
Australian scam losses totalled $2.18 billion in 2025
with AFCA beginning to handle scam complaints from 1 January 2027
notes: Trade press report on a government regime; the Treasury exposure draft (27/05/2026) was read but falls outside the anchor allowance, so this report carries the Australian evidence. Age 95 days (soft 90-day window).

title: APP fraud reimbursement: the evaluation verdict
date_evidence: By Rob Bratby Posted on 6 July 2026 4 August 2026
key_claim: The PSR's own data show 30% of fraud by value and 69% by volume originates via online platforms; reimbursement rates range from 21% to 94% across PSPs; out-of-scope international scams rose from £21m to £60m; a formal consultation is due in December 2026 and revised directions in May 2027.
frame_summary: The specialist law-firm commentary reads the evaluation as proof of effect but flags that the cost sits on payment firms while the fraud originates elsewhere.
verbatim_quote: 30% of fraud by value and 69% by volume originates via online platforms
verbatim_list: Frontier found reimbursement rates ranging from 21% to 94% across PSPs
international APP scams, which fall outside the requirement, rose from £21m in 2023 to £60m in 2025
a formal consultation in December 2026, and a decision with revised legal directions in May 2027
the requirement places incentives on PSPs alone
